summary: How to deal with deep-level diffuse accumulation (lossless+speed-neutral) AND what tree-reshape space is actually reachable+useful given cat10(wider)=no-help and the MTP drafter capabilities

approaches.name: Replay-route exact re-anchoring (already built, live-PASS at 02b1627a)
approaches.what: After each accept event, do NOT carry the chunk-vs-recurrent scan's accumulated fp32 state forward as h0. Instead recompute the committed deep-node state by RE-EXECUTING the accepted root-to-leaf path through the identical rank-1 _gdn_node_step body from a tiny activation ring (k pre-l2norm, v, raw_a, raw_b at consumed precision), publishing post-step states straight to the bank's LINEAR columns. This is the literal 'recompute the verified state from cached input activations in a separate state-update pass' of Snakes-and-Ladders / SpecPV periodic-refresh. It resets per-event accumulation to the native recurrent realization (the replay runs in the NATIVE gate-folding basis, no rescaled-exp), so deep-position drift cannot ratchet across events the way it does when a drifted accumulator is reused. Code: _tree_gdn_replay_kernel + launch_tree_gdn_replay in fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py; glue + the page-safe conv remap fix in fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py. ALREADY exists, byte-proven offline (126/126 Gate A) AND live-PASS in both eager+captured regimes after the conv-page-stride wiring fix (02b1627a, FR13_REPLAY_GPU_GATES_BIND ADDENDUM).
approaches.losslessSafe: YES by construction — it re-runs the SAME shared _gdn_node_step on bit-identical ring inputs in native's gate-folding basis; it does not deviate shared/native machinery, it aligns OUR cross-event handoff to native's. Byte-A/B proven incl. two-event chains. Caveat: re-gate the FULL chain (corruption gate + B=4 captured SWE-4 vs E5) before claiming lossless e2e — it was only walked to live-gate-PASS, not to the final regime.
approaches.speedImpact: NEUTRAL-to-POSITIVE on GEMV-bound B=1. It REPLACES the 36-row/forward all-node HBM state export (21.74 GB, 5.14x native traffic) with a 6-row replay (3.62 GB, 0.86x native) + ~16 KiB/node ring. 0-spill, 48 regs. The replay scan itself is a tiny latency sliver. Net: cuts the dominant memory-traffic cost, not adds.
approaches.appliesIf: both — it re-anchors the cross-event h0 handoff (kernel-handoff outcome, chain5~22) directly; under the co-residency outcome (chain5~3) it still helps because it gives the committed spine column a native-realization state instead of the drifted scan checkpoint.

approaches.name: Co-residency isolation: compute path-0 spine in a chain-identical instruction path
approaches.what: If chain5~3 (leaves/co-residency are the excess), make the committed spine rows bit-identical to a pure 5-chain. The scan kernel is ALREADY structurally separable: in _tree_gdn_kernel each node i resumes from b_h0 then overlays ONLY its ancestors' h_cache via strict_mask (`ancestor=(strict_mask[i,j]!=0)&(j<N_ACTUAL)`); there is no tl.sum/reduction that folds non-ancestor (branch) rows into a spine node. So a spine node's arithmetic depends only on its spine ancestors. The isolation 'fix' is therefore to (a) verify the spine column's published/committed state is the one produced by the spine-only ancestry walk (it is, since branch leaves are never ancestors of spine nodes), and (b) if any residual co-residency shows up, run the path-0 spine through a SEPARATE single-spine launch (is_single_spine path / a depth-5 chain launch) so its codegen + reduction tree is byte-identical to native's chain — branches in their own launch.
approaches.losslessSafe: YES — spine-only computation is the SpecInfer Def 4.1 / STree path-rerun oracle for the committed path; isolating it removes nothing the committed token depends on. Branch nodes remain lossless via their own root-to-path ancestry (already correct).
approaches.speedImpact: NEUTRAL if kept in one launch (no change). If split into a separate spine launch it adds one small extra kernel launch (negligible at B=1 GEMV-bound) but the spine launch is depth-5xV-heads — a latency sliver. No GEMM/GEMV regression.

approaches.name: h0-handoff realization alignment to native bf16 single-slot
approaches.what: Native rolls a single recurrent state slot in-place (bf16). Our path keeps an fp32 MULTI-COLUMN bank and reads h0 from the accepted column clamp(prev_len-1,0) (h0_use_accepted_column=True). If chain5~22, align OUR h0 read to native's realization: the replay route already does this (publishes native-basis fp32 to the linear column the next event reads). The remaining knob is whether to keep the bank in fp32 (more precise than native bf16) or round the published handoff to bf16 to MATCH native's realization. Given GDN sub-ops are already bit-exact and the bar is per-depth-argmax within native's self-floor (not abs-0.0), keep fp32 (strictly more precise) UNLESS the e2e argmax probe shows fp32-vs-bf16 tips a flip — then match native bf16 at the handoff only.
approaches.losslessSafe: YES — fp32 bank is a lossless IMPROVEMENT (more precise than native's bf16 slot), so it cannot lose information vs native; it can only be a REALIZATION mismatch. The replay's native-basis publish is the alignment. Matching to bf16 is also lossless-safe (it only equals native's own realization).
approaches.speedImpact: NEUTRAL — fp32 vs bf16 bank read is a tiny load; no GEMV impact. The replay already pays the publish cost.

approaches.name: Leaner / shallower committed tree (chain5/cat7/cat8) to cut depth-accumulation
approaches.what: The diffuse drift grows MONOTONICALLY with committed-spine depth (born L0 GDN, ratchets L41-L63). A shallower committed spine = fewer rank-1 chunk-vs-recurrent steps before re-anchoring = less accumulation per event. The TREE env var is free (list-of-tuples, num_spec auto-derived), so chain5/cat7/cat8 subsets are buildable with no retrain. NOTE the WIDER direction is empirically DEAD (cat10: 22 flips redistributed not reduced, accept 3.198->2.932 worse, +1.3% s/fwd). The OPEN lever is LEANER/shallower only.
approaches.losslessSafe: YES — reshaping the candidate tree changes only WHICH tokens are proposed/verified; each verified node is still lossless via its own ancestry. No shared/native machinery deviated.
approaches.speedImpact: NEUTRAL-to-POSITIVE — fewer verify rows = smaller lm-head GEMV over the verify set; but shallower spine risks lower accept/event (depth gives cat9 its accept edge). This is the flips-vs-accept frontier the user wants measured, not self-closed.
approaches.appliesIf: both — fewer deep positions reduces accumulation regardless of whether the carrier is co-residency or handoff.

approaches.name: Numerical per-op alignment (NOT applicable — already exhausted)
approaches.what: The classic 'diffuse = a few un-aligned seams' decomposition (conv bf16-tap, scan static_range unroll, intra-chunk A cast) that previously dissolved diffuse walls. For FR13 this is DONE: GDN sub-ops conv/scan/gate/o_proj/in_proj are individually bit-exact to native (FR12), and the GDN-scan launch-geometry (BV/warps) hypothesis is MEASURED-FALSE (RAW max_abs==0.0 vs native at all geometries incl deployed N_PAD=16, FR13_BV_GEOMETRY_NOT_THE_SEAM). The DIM_K reduction is geometry-invariant. So there is NO remaining per-op/geometry numerical seam to round — do not re-open this line.
approaches.losslessSafe: N/A — no further per-op alignment available; sub-ops already bit-exact.
approaches.appliesIf: both — but vacuous: the per-forward GDN computation is already bit-exact, so the carrier is cross-event handoff or co-residency, NOT a per-op seam.

dd.reAnchoring: YES — and it is ALREADY BUILT as the replay route, and it is the single strongest answer here. Mechanism: instead of feeding the next event's h0 from the tree scan's drifted fp32 checkpoint, recompute the committed deep-node state by re-executing the accepted root-to-leaf path through the identical rank-1 _gdn_node_step body from a small persistent activation ring (k pre-l2norm, v, raw_a, raw_b at the precision actually consumed), in native's gate-folding basis, publishing post-step states directly to the bank's LINEAR columns (column t = t-th accepted token; root always to column 0 for the zero-accept case). This is the textbook 'recompute the verified state from cached input activations with a separate state-update kernel' of Snakes-and-Ladders, and the periodic-full-refresh idea of SpecPV — it resets accumulation to the native recurrent realization every event, so deep-position drift cannot ratchet across events. Lossless-by-construction: same shared body, bit-identical ring inputs, native basis — byte-A/B proven offline (Gate A 126/126; old-vs-new scan binary byte-equal; two-event handoff chains byte-equal). Cost at B=1 is a NET REDUCTION, not addition: it deletes the scan's per-node HBM state export (36 rows/forward -> 6, 21.74 GB -> 3.62 GB, 5.14x native traffic -> 0.86x), with a ~16 KiB/node ring and a spill-free 48-reg replay kernel — exactly the GEMV-bound win you want. STATUS: the live gate-4 collapse (accept 2.02->1.58, non-determinism) was ROOT-CAUSED to a pure-WIRING bug (the conv-half linear remap copied stride(0)=whole-page elements over the just-published ssm linear columns, because conv/ssm kv are as_strided views over the SAME mamba page) and FIXED at commit 02b1627a via a page-safe torch remap (kernel untouched); re-gate now PASSES in BOTH eager and captured regimes (4/4 same-seed determinism, accept 2.08/2.15, CUDA-graph-captures clean). REMAINING before lossless e2e claim: it was walked to live-gate-PASS, not to the FINAL regime — still owes the corruption gate + B=4 FULL-capture SWE-4 vs E5 (within E5 self-noise + accept/event >= native 3.076). Branch fr13-replay-route, NOT merged (user decision class). This is the lossless+speed-neutral re-anchoring the task asks for, and it is mostly done.
dd.coResidencyIsolation: YES — the spine rows CAN be computed bit-identically to a pure chain, and the scan kernel is already structurally separable. Read of _tree_gdn_kernel (fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:459-527): each node i initializes state_i = b_h0, then for j<i overlays ONLY ancestor states via `ancestor=(tl.load(strict_mask+i*N_PAD+j)!=0)&(j<N_ACTUAL)`; h_j is gathered with `tl.sum(tl.where(offs_n==j, h_cache, 0.0),axis=0)` (a SELECT of one cached row, not a cross-row mix). There is NO reduction or tl.sum that folds non-ancestor (branch) rows into a spine node's state or output. Therefore a spine node's arithmetic depends solely on its spine ancestors' h_cache checkpoints + its own activations — branch leaves are never ancestors of a spine node, so they cannot perturb it. CONSEQUENCE: path-0 spine is ALREADY isolated from branch rows within the kernel; co-residency cannot contaminate the spine through the GDN scan math (it could only contaminate via a SHARED-ACCUMULATOR design — which is exactly STree's no-copy degradation that this kernel deliberately avoids by per-node h_cache checkpointing, the reference_multispine 'shared recurrent state contaminates spine-0' failure mode that is NOT present here). If chain5~3 nonetheless implicates co-residency, the residual must be in co-residency of the BATCHED forward OUTSIDE the GDN scan (e.g. fp8 GEMM/full-attn batch-variance across the wider token set), addressable by (a) confirming the committed spine state equals the spine-only ancestry walk, and if needed (b) launching path-0 through a separate single-spine launch (Tree.is_single_spine path) so its codegen/reduction tree matches native's depth-5 chain byte-for-byte, with branches in their own launch. Lossless: spine-only = the SpecInfer/STree path-rerun oracle for the committed path. Speed: one extra small launch at most (negligible, GEMV-bound). Graph-capture: both single-spine and tree launches are already capture-safe (preallocated masks/out/state).
dd.h0HandoffAlign: Our fp32 multi-column bank is a lossless IMPROVEMENT over native's bf16 single-slot in-place roll (fp32 carries strictly more precision than bf16), so it cannot LOSE information relative to native — it can only be a REALIZATION MISMATCH that tips an argmax. The replay route already realizes the alignment: it publishes post-step states in native's gate-folding basis (no rescaled-exp reconstruction) directly to the LINEAR column the next event reads (h0 column = clamp(prev_len-1,0), matching the scan's in-kernel h0 gather; root always published to column 0 for zero-accept). What native does across events: rolls one slot in place per accepted token (bf16), reading h0 = the last accepted token's state. Our convention reads the SAME logical column (accepted_len-1) — already aligned in index space. RECOMMENDATION: KEEP fp32 (more precise, and the GDN sub-ops are bit-exact so the fp32 bank does not introduce a per-op seam), and let the replay's native-basis publish carry the realization alignment — DO NOT round the handoff to bf16 unless the binding per-token argmax-vs-clean probe shows the fp32-vs-bf16 handoff difference actually tips a flip at a deep committed position (the bar is per-depth-argmax within native's 3-flip self-floor, NOT abs-0.0, per the 2026-06-09 ruling). If a flip is traced to the fp32 handoff, match native bf16 AT THE HANDOFF PUBLISH ONLY (still lossless-safe: it equals native's own realization), keeping the in-scan fp32 accumulation. Note: the prior gate-4 collapse was NOT an fp32-vs-bf16 issue — it was the conv-page-stride wiring bug, now fixed; do not misattribute it to the bank dtype.
dd.priorArt: DIRECTLY ON-POINT: (1) Snakes-and-Ladders (Amazon Science, 2024) — the canonical SSM-spec-decode state-handling: SSM intermediate states are not in HBM and cannot be recovered from the final state, so the committed state MUST be RECOMPUTED; they recompute the verified state at the last-accepted position via a SEPARATE forward pass over cached input activations focused on the state-update kernel (hardware-aware, avoids storing the large state to HBM each step). This is EXACTLY the FR13 replay route — strongest validation that re-anchoring-by-recompute is the correct, established mechanism. (2) STree (arXiv 2505.14969, NeurIPS 2025) — first scalable tree-spec for hybrid SSMs; checkpoints at acceptance boundaries and treats each accept as a RESTART point (re-anchor), and crucially branches track their OWN recurrent evolution anchored to a common spine checkpoint rather than a fully shared accumulator (matches the per-node h_cache isolation in our kernel; the shared-accumulator path is what degrades path0, the project_gdn_tree_superset_routes / reference_multispine root cause). Does NOT analyze fp-drift/chunk-vs-recurrent realization. (3) SpecPV (arXiv 2512.02337) — periodic FULL verification to ELIMINATE accumulated errors and refresh partial state; the periodic-exact-re-anchoring pattern generalized. (4) SpecInfer (tree attention, root-to-leaf path verification, Def 4.1 path-rerun = the branch-node losslessness oracle) + Sequoia (arXiv 2402.12374, hardware-aware tree shape as constrained optimization — relevant to the lean/shallow reshape lever) + EAGLE-2/3 (dynamic/static trees, structured ancestry mask = independent parallel per-path verification, no cross-branch attention). (5) Attention-Drift (arXiv 2605.09992) — deep-chain error accumulation grows monotonically with chain depth via the un-normalized residual path; post-norm tolerates ~10x more per-step perturbation than pre-norm (mechanistic backing for the depth-accumulation being real and for shallower committed depth reducing it). (6) DeltaNet chunkwise (Yang et al. arXiv 2406.06484) + Gated DeltaNet — the chunkwise-parallel vs recurrent forms are mathematically equivalent but numerically differ (fused = less precise); the FR13 residual is precisely this chunk-vs-recurrent realization gap of the recurrent state in the tree forward. No paper claims a lower bound on the lossy-ness, consistent with native being the 7x-better existence proof.
dd.ranked:
Ranked by lossless-safe AND speed-neutral AND small, conditioned on chain5 outcome:

#1 (BOTH outcomes, regardless of chain5): FINISH THE REPLAY-ROUTE RE-ANCHORING (fr13-replay-route @ 02b1627a). It is the lossless-by-construction, speed-POSITIVE (cuts native traffic 5.14x->0.86x), already-built, byte-A/B-proven, live-gate-PASS answer. It directly addresses the kernel-handoff carrier and de-risks the co-residency one (gives the committed spine a native-realization state). 'Small' = it's done through live-gate-PASS; remaining work is GATES not BUILD (corruption gate + B=4 captured SWE-4 vs E5). This is the recommendation under BOTH chain5 outcomes.

#2 IF chain5~3 (co-residency is the excess): SPINE ISOLATION VERIFICATION first (free — the kernel is already separable; just confirm the committed spine column equals the spine-only ancestry walk via a CPU/eager check), then only if a residual remains, the separate single-spine launch for path-0 (one tiny extra launch, lossless, capture-safe). Cheaper than #1 to TEST, but #1 still needed for the cross-event handoff.

#3 IF chain5~22 (kernel/handoff on a pure chain differs): the replay route (#1) IS the fix; additionally KEEP fp32 bank, align handoff realization via the native-basis publish, and only fall back to bf16-at-handoff if the per-token argmax probe traces a flip to fp32-vs-bf16 (small, lossless-safe).

#4 (BOTH, complementary, defer): LEANER/shallower committed tree (chain5/cat7/cat8) to cut depth-accumulation at the source — lossless, plausibly speed-positive, but trades against accept/event (the flips-vs-accept frontier the user wants measured, not self-closed). WIDER is DEAD (cat10). Do AFTER #1, as the reshape sweep through the B=1 SWE gold gate.

NOT RANKED / EXCLUDED: per-op or BV-geometry numerical alignment (sub-ops already bit-exact, geometry MEASURED-FALSE — do not re-open); copy-recurrent multi-spine / dense / splice (reward-hacks, banned).

rs.reachableShapes:
REACHABLE SHAPE SPACE — two independent gates, both must pass:

(A) GDN VERIFY KERNEL — accepts ANY tree up to 16 total nodes. The strict/visible ancestry masks are built generically from the env tree_choices at init: parent[node]=index[choice[:-1]], strict[node,anc]=1 via ancestry walk (scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:215-242). The ONLY cap is n_pad = 1<<(n-1).bit_length(); raise if n_pad>16 (src/.../fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:75-78 and patch :226-231). NODE_FAMILIES=(2,3,6,8,14) and make_tree() are WARMUP-only fixtures, NOT a runtime constraint — cat9(9) and cat10(10) both run, proving runtime topology is data-driven from the mask. So root-siblings, wider, leaner, and rank>=2 trees are ALL verify-kernel-legal as long as total nodes <=16. Confirmed cat10 root-sibling+wider ran (FR13_CAT10_BIND.md, engagement PASS, draft-toks/event=10.0).

(B) DRAFTER — the BINDING constraint, and it is HAND-ROLLED per shape, not general. propose() (patch :9657-10558) has hardcoded packings that fire ONLY on exact-match of tree_choices: cat9 (_fr10_caterpillar_choices, 9 nodes, :9670), chain5/spine-only (_fr10_spine_only_choices, 5 nodes, :9675), and cat10 (a separate _fr10_is_caterpillar10 branch added on the cat10 experiment branch, NOT on main HEAD — git log f8a9c032/31e227cf; the cat10 raw-wf shows it stacks [spine0,ROOT_LEAF,spine1,leaf0,...] with ROOT_LEAF=topk(root_logits,2)[:,1]). ANY non-matching shape hits the guard at :10567-10580 and RAISES ("FR10 caterpillar drafter disengaged") unless FR10_ALLOW_LINEAR_FALLBACK=1, which routes to native propose_tree (:10618). So today, only {chain5, cat9} are wired on main; cat10 needed branch code. New shapes need EITHER (i) a few-line hardcoded packing like cat10, or (ii) the native propose_tree fallback path. Both are no-retrain.

Net: root-sibling = CONFIRMED reachable+ran (cat10). Leaner subsets chain5/cat7/cat8 = verify-legal; chain5 wired, cat7/cat8 need a small packing add. rank>=2 = verify-legal AND drafter-feasible via native propose_tree topk (see rankKFeasible).
rs.rankKFeasible:
YES — rank>=2 (top-3+) children are buildable with NO retrain. Two independent confirmations:

1. NATIVE propose_tree (the fallback path, live vLLM eagle.py:936-1110) selects children by torch.topk(logits, num_children, dim=-1).indices where num_children = child_drafts_per_level[level] = num_drafts_per_level[level] // num_drafts_per_level[level-1] (eagle.py:263-273). The MTP head emits FULL-vocab logits, so topk for any k is just an index read — no weights, no retrain. The path-tuple's LAST integer IS the rank: the patch's own consumption recorder decodes _fr10_rank = int(choice[-1]) and validates flat_col = parent_slot*num_children + rank against topk(level_logits, num_children) (patch :10711-10722). So a tree with (0,2) or (0,0,2) (3rd-ranked child) is consumed as topk rank-2 directly.

2. The cat10 hardcoded drafter ALREADY took a rank-1 sibling from topk(root_logits,2)[:,1] with NO extra lm-head read (reused the materialized root logits) — demonstrating the head already carries the full distribution; extending to [:,2] (rank-2) is a one-index change.

GATING CODE: nothing gates top-k beyond (a) the hardcoded packings only emitting rank-0 (spine argmax) + rank-1 (leaf top2[:,1]) for the cat shapes (patch :10112,:10120 — _fr10_step_top2[:,1]), and (b) the per-level UNIFORMITY constraint baked into native propose_tree's flat layout: num_children is an integer (cu_drafts // prev_level), so ALL parents at a given level must have the SAME child count for the flat topk layout to be valid (eagle.py:272-273 integer division; non-uniform fan-out per level is NOT expressible). Cost/benefit: rank-2 via native fallback = zero new code (set FR10_ALLOW_LINEAR_FALLBACK=1 + a tree with rank-2 nodes); via hardcoded packing = ~10 lines like cat10. Benefit is questionable (see leanerHypothesis/recommendation): rank-2 root siblings rescue shallow rejects but cat10's rank-1 root sibling already showed width REDISTRIBUTES not REDUCES flips and HURT accept.
rs.leanerHypothesis:
The LEANER lever can plausibly cut flips, but the COST is accept/event, and the math is tight against the 3.16 bar.

MECHANISM (why leaner cuts flips): The 22 flips are DIFFUSE per-layer GDN realization drift, BORN at L0 (~3.9e-3), growing MONOTONICALLY with committed-spine DEPTH to L63 (FR13_DIFFUSE_GDN_EXPLAINED.md; substitution test: splice oracle@L58 reverts, @L0 doesn't). The decisive_flip_targets are DEPTH-4 SPINE nodes (FR13_BASELINE_RESOLVED_BIND.md). So the flips ride the DEEPEST committed spine positions. cat9's 22 flips per-prompt [5,7,4,6]; cat10 redistributed to [2,6,8,6] but stayed 22 — width does nothing because it doesn't touch committed DEPTH. SHORTENING THE SPINE (dropping deep nodes (0,0,0,0) / (0,0,0,0,0)) directly removes the positions where flips are most likely committed AND caps the max committed depth, which is exactly the accumulation that ratchets. This is the only lever aligned with the carrier.

COST (why it fights the bar): cat9's accept edge comes FROM the deep accepts. Per-depth accept rates (FR13_CAT10_BIND.md): cat9 d0=0.871 d1=0.828 d2=0.638 d3=0.483 d4=0.379. accept/event = 0.871+0.828+0.638+0.483+0.379 = ~3.20. Drop d4 (cat8-spine, depth-4): lose the 0.379 expected accept => accept/event ~= 2.82. Drop d3+d4 (cat-depth-3): ~= 2.34. BOTH fall BELOW native 3.16. So a pure spine-shortening that removes deep nodes ALSO removes the accept they contribute — and the deep accepts are worth MORE than the flip reduction in accept terms. chain5 (the running control) = depth-5 spine, NO leaves: it keeps full depth (so keeps the deep-flip carrier) but drops the 4 leaves (which contribute the d1-d4 LEAF accepts, ~0.5-0.8 of the per-event yield) => chain5 will be LOWER accept than cat9 AND keep most flips (depth unchanged). 

CONCLUSION ON LEANER: NO lean SUBSET of cat9 can simultaneously hit ~3 flips and >=3.16 accept. The flips live on deep spine depth; the accept also lives on deep depth. You cannot drop the deep nodes to cut flips without dropping below 3.16 accept. The ONLY way leaner could win is if the deep-LEAF nodes (not spine) carry disproportionate flips while the deep-SPINE accepts carry the accept — but the evidence says the opposite (flip targets are deep SPINE, and leaves are off-spine so they don't ratchet the recurrent state). The lean frontier is a LOSE-LOSE for the bar; it should still be MEASURED (chain5 is running) but the prediction is it does not clear native-3+accept-3.16.
rs.smarterTopology:
Yes, several non-obvious shapes worth a GPU gate, but each fights the same depth-vs-accept tension; none clearly clears BOTH bars on the diffuse mechanism:

1. SHORTER SPINE + COMPENSATING WIDTH AT SHALLOW DEPTHS (e.g. depth-3 spine + rank-2/rank-3 siblings at d0,d1,d2). Bounds max committed depth at 3 (cuts the deepest-spine flip carrier + caps accumulation) while recovering accept via shallow breadth where accept rates are HIGH (d0=0.87,d1=0.83,d2=0.64). This is the ONLY shape that attacks flips (depth cap) AND defends accept (shallow width) at once. Reachable: verify-kernel-legal (<=16 nodes), needs native propose_tree fallback (non-uniform fan-out NOT expressible in the flat layout — must keep per-level child count uniform, so e.g. 1 root with 2 children, each with 2 children = balanced binary depth-3 = 1+2+4+8=15 nodes <=16 OK). BUT cat10 already showed adding ANY width hurt deeper accept (d1-d4 ALL dropped when the root sibling was added: dilution/co-residency), so the accept recovery is UNCERTAIN. WORTH ONE GATE — it is the strongest non-obvious candidate.
